feature.title: Milestone M2 — KeepLab email/password auth + single-user note sync
feature.summary: One milestone contract covering sequential A3 (email/password registration, email verification, password login, password reset, JWT access token, opaque retry-safe rotating refresh token, logout, per-session revoke, Android Keystore-backed session store, minimal account/auth UI) followed by A4 (Room outbox + client checkpoint, stable UUIDs for independently synced children, backend sync tables, POST /v1/sync/mutations + GET /v1/sync/changes with atomic mutation-id dedupe, server revision authority with 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, tombstone != Trash, failed-delta checkpoint rule, non-destructive 404 rule, explicit accountId invariant, and one unique WorkManager note_sync pipeline). One contract, one execution session, one final verification pass. No device, no cloud, no attachments, no collaboration, no account deletion, no automatic Trash purge, no conflict-resolution UI, no A5 hardening.

purpose: This package is a TEMPORARY EXECUTION CONTRACT covering the whole M2 milestone (A3 + A4). It exists so that a later fresh session can implement A3 and then A4 through the SAME unmodified Contract Guard, under an explicit and bounded write surface, with A3 and A4 kept as logically separate checkpoints inside ONE session and ONE final verification pass. This contract-creation task performed targeted discovery and authored the package; it does not implement M2.

milestone.flow: PLAN ONCE -> A3 EXECUTE -> A3 LIGHT CHECKPOINT -> CONTINUE DIRECTLY TO A4 -> A4 EXECUTE -> VERIFY M2 ONCE -> PASS = STOP
milestone.a3_is_not_a_stop: A3_CHECKPOINT is a checkpoint, not a Review. The session must not stop at it, must not create an A3 contract, must not create an A3 review.
milestone.logical_boundary: A3 code belongs to A3; note sync is never described as part of A3. A4 code begins only after the A3 checkpoint. The phase boundary is preserved without stopping the session.

human_authorization_source.decision_effect: The three M2-blocking human decisions are explicitly approved by the human project owner on 2026-10-06. D-01 fixes the auth method (email + password, email verification required, password login, password reset; passkey may come later; phone deferred; Google login and Firebase Auth forbidden). D-04 fixes the sign-out policy as PRESERVE_LOCAL_CACHE (non-destructive: local Room data, account-scoped cached notes, the outbox and LOCAL_ONLY notes all survive sign-out; no full Room database encryption is claimed or authorized). D-10 fixes the token model (short-lived JWT access token plus an opaque high-entropy rotating refresh token with a retry-safe refresh_request_id replay window, refresh secrets never stored plaintext).
human_authorization_source.stale_wording_elsewhere: MINOR_BACKLOG, not a blocker (for example reports/KEEPLAB-AUTH-SYNC-HUMAN-DECISIONS.md and reports/KEEPLAB-AUTH-SYNC-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md §23.1 still list D-01/D-04/D-10 as pending).

boundary_notes.resolution: allowed_paths / forbidden_paths are project-relative to the Contract Guard's project-context source_root, exactly as the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract and the A0/A1/A2 contracts are. Entries may be exact files or directory prefixes.
boundary_notes.precedence: The guard tests forbidden_paths first; a path matching both lists is BLOCKED. reports/ is allowed while reports/contracts/ (which contains this package and every earlier package) is forbidden, so an executor cannot write its own contract or any historical package.
boundary_notes.unlisted_is_blocked: Any path inside the project root that matches neither list is BLOCKED (UNCLASSIFIED_FAIL_CLOSED).
boundary_notes.android_surface_is_enumerated_not_whole_: KeepLab-Relay/app/** is NOT authorized as a whole. The authorized Android surface is the enumerated persistence/data package, the DI package, the model package, the named UI packages that carry auth/account state and the note/label/checklist read-write paths, the application and activity entry points, AndroidManifest.xml, app/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/src/test/**. Everything else under app/ — themes, shared UI widgets, resources, androidTest, benchmark, schemas, proguard rules — is BLOCKED.
boundary_notes.android_surface_rationale: A3/A4 genuinely need new packages (data/auth, data/remote, data/sync, a Keystore-backed session store, ui/auth, ui/settings) plus edits to the single repository/creation boundary, the DAOs, the database, the DI wiring, the navigation graph and the note/label/checklist UI that calls those boundaries. A whole-app authorization is therefore not required and is not granted.
boundary_notes.root_gradle_blocked: settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties, gradle/wrapper/** and gradlew are forbidden. Only app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml may change, and only to add the dependencies M2 needs without removing or gratuitously bumping unrelated entries. A needed root Gradle change is a STOP with M2_ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE_REQUIRED.
boundary_notes.backend_surface_is_whole_directory: The whole KeepLab-Relay/backend/ prefix is authorized, so ordinary compile fixes, added source files, backend-local Gradle files, resources and new Flyway migrations never require another contract.
boundary_notes.cloud_blocked: No cloud, infra, server or firebase path is authorized; the existing backend Docker assets stay untouched in content and are never executed.
boundary_notes.device_blocked: No Android device access and no adb. androidTest and benchmark source are read-only and are never executed.
boundary_notes.out_of_project: Paths outside /mnt/AndroidDev/Projects remain OUT_OF_CONTRACT_SCOPE/ALLOW as the guard is written today; this contract does not change that guard property and must never be read as authorizing writes outside the project.
boundary_notes.guard_scope_note: The frozen guard classifies WRITE targets, not tool choice: it has no path rule that blocks an `adb` binary, `./gradlew`, `docker compose` or a container run, and it cannot classify Hermes config/core paths outside the project root. The device prohibition, the cloud prohibitions, the Google/Firebase prohibition and the Hermes-core prohibition are enforced by this contract's declarations and the execution prompt's stop conditions, not by the path list. Violating one is a CONTRACT_DEVIATION. This limitation is stated rather than hidden.
boundary_notes.hermes_config_core_limitation: Hermes configuration and core live OUTSIDE the guard's source_root (/home/zhong/.hermes/...), so the guard's path lists cannot classify them. They are protected here by an explicit hard prohibition and stop condition, enforced by fail-closed operator discipline — not by the path list.

requirements.statement: D-01 is honoured: email+password registration with required email verification, password login, and password reset; no Google/Firebase/phone/OAuth-social identity exists anywhere.
The backend gains a development PostgreSQL/Flyway schema for users, email verification challenges, password reset challenges, sessions and refresh-rotation state, and nothing beyond what A3 requires.

A modern password KDF (Argon2id preferred, never hand-rolled) protects passwords, and verification/reset codes are stored only in a secure verifier/hash form with a delivery abstraction (fake sender in tests, development-only console sender).
The versioned A3 auth API works end to end: register, verify-email, login, refresh, logout, list sessions, per-session revoke, password-reset request and confirm.
The access token is a short-lived JWT whose identity is server-derived (sub/sid/iat/exp/iss/aud), signed with a key from environment/config and never from source code.

The refresh token is opaque and high-entropy, stored server-side only as a safe verifier/hash, rotated on use, and retry-safe by refresh_request_id within a bounded replay window with no plaintext secret result retained.

The Android client implements register/verify/login/refresh/logout/session state and stores access and refresh material only in an app-private Android Keystore-backed secure store, without claiming Room database encryption.

A minimal account/auth UI is reachable (sign in, register, verify email, forgot/reset password, signed-in account state, sign out) through a settings/account area, and the app remains fully usable without login.

D-04 is honoured: sign-out clears session credentials and active-account state, stops sync, and preserves Room data, account-scoped cached notes, the outbox and LOCAL_ONLY notes; AUTH_REQUIRED never deletes local data.

Pre-existing LOCAL_ONLY notes are never silently assigned, uploaded, deleted or merged into an account; a new signed-out note stays LOCAL_ONLY and a new signed-in note becomes account-scoped SYNC_PENDING.

The Room model supports single-account sync: stable UUIDs for independently synced checklist items and labels, an outbox table, a client checkpoint table and the minimum indexing required, with a direct experimental schema bump and local Long PKs kept where useful.

A persistent Room outbox records mutationId, accountId, target client UUID, mutation kind, baseRevision, payload and createdAt plus only the minimal A4 status fields, written in the same local transaction as the entity mutation.

The backend gains new Flyway migrations after V1 for notes, checklist items, labels, note-label relations, server revision, sync tombstones, the server change log/cursor and mutation-id dedupe — with no attachments, no collaboration, no multi-account and no CRDT.
The sync API exists at /v1/sync/mutations, /v1/sync/changes?since=<cursor> and /v1/sync/checkpoint, authenticated only by the access JWT, never trusting a request accountId as authority.
A duplicate mutation_id never applies twice: the dedupe claim and the mutation application are atomic in one transaction, and a duplicate returns the already-applied result.

The server is the revision authority: an accepted mutation advances the server revision, a stale baseRevision yields 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, and the client marks the entity CONFLICT and stops destructive overwrite without any conflict-resolution UI.
Client wall clock is never conflict authority; ordering and conflict authority are the server revision and the server-accepted change order.
Trash stays reversible product Trash and is synced as ordinary note state; a final deletion is a tombstone; M2 does not auto-purge tombstones or Trash, and a deleted remote note does not resurrect.

The server change cursor and the client checkpoint are distinct; the checkpoint advances only after a clean transactional apply of the returned page, and a failed delta leaves the checkpoint unchanged.
A server 404 never deletes a live local note; it maps to a non-destructive sync/error state.
Any entity in a remote-sync state has a non-null accountId; LOCAL_ONLY is the only state that may have a null accountId, enforced at creation/update boundaries and by deterministic tests.

Exactly one unique WorkManager note_sync pipeline exists, with an ExistingWorkPolicy chosen as an A4 implementation decision and shown by deterministic tests not to create parallel duplicate pipelines; triggers fire after an account-scoped mutation, after login, on a foreground/app-start entry and from a manual entry; no push provider or FCM exists.

The worker flow ensures a valid session, refreshes when necessary, pushes pending mutations, handles responses, pulls changes after the checkpoint, applies them into Room, advances the checkpoint only after success, and is mapped so that auth, network and temporary server failures never lose local data and a generic 5xx is not treated as permanent by default.
A4 syncs note create, title/body edit, archive, pin, colour, Trash state, checklist changes and label changes, both directions, with Room remaining the local SSOT that the UI reads.

The milestone is verified in exactly one pass with both frozen gates run once; a failure is fixed on the failed path only and only the failed task re-runs; the Android app builds and the backend builds with their relevant tests passing.

tasks.goal: A3 Android: Keystore-backed session store, auth/session client repository, auth API client, and the minimal account/auth UI plus navigation/settings entry.
tasks.boundary: Only the enumerated Android surface in allowed_paths. Room entity/DAO changes required by A3 only. No sync worker.
tasks.verification: Android JVM tests cover refresh/session repository behaviour, sign-out preserving local data and outbox, and LOCAL_ONLY filtering. The app compiles with :app:assembleDebug semantics preserved for the final gate.
tasks.done_when: Tokens live only in an app-private Keystore-backed store; the INTERNET permission is present; register/verify/login/refresh/logout/session state are implemented; sign-in, register, verify email, forgot/reset password, signed-in state and sign-out are reachable from the account/settings area; the app is still usable without login; no Google/Firebase path exists.

tasks.goal: A3 light checkpoint — record the checkpoint state and continue directly to A4.
tasks.boundary: Reporting only. No new contract, no review, no session stop.
tasks.verification: A short checkpoint record states: A3 backend auth structures authored; Android auth/session structures authored; human D-01/D-04/D-10 honoured; no Google/Firebase auth; local data still non-destructive.
tasks.done_when: A3_CHECKPOINT: READY_FOR_A4 is recorded and the session continues into A4 without running the Milestone gate.

tasks.goal: A4 local Room model: schema bump with client UUIDs for checklist items and labels, outbox table, client checkpoint table, minimum indexes, and the DAO/database wiring.
tasks.boundary: Only the enumerated Android persistence surface plus DI. No backend file. No SyncManager yet.
tasks.verification: Deterministic JVM tests assert the fresh-row defaults, outbox record creation, the checkpoint table shape and the accountId invariant. The direct experimental schema bump is recorded with DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES.
tasks.done_when: ChecklistItemEntity and LabelEntity carry stable unique client UUIDs; an outbox table and a client checkpoint table exist with the required fields; local Long PKs are kept where useful; the schema version is bumped directly with no migration chain authored.

tasks.goal: A4 write path: enqueue outbox rows in the same transaction as each account-scoped mutation, account-scoped filtering, and LOCAL_ONLY safety.
tasks.verification: Deterministic JVM tests: LOCAL_ONLY before login; sign-out preserves Room data and the outbox; inactive-account rows are not reassigned; a signed-in new note becomes account scoped; outbox creation; remote-sync rows always carry a non-null accountId.
tasks.done_when: Every note/label/checklist mutation from the repository boundary creates the matching outbox row in one local transaction; signed-out UI shows LOCAL_ONLY only; signed-in UI shows LOCAL_ONLY plus the active account's rows; pre-login notes are never adopted.

tasks.goal: A4 Android sync engine: one unique WorkManager note_sync pipeline, push/pull worker, error mapping, checkpoint discipline and the manual/foreground/login triggers.
tasks.verification: Deterministic JVM tests with a fake backend/MockEngine: push success; pull success; 409 -> CONFLICT; 404 does not delete; a failed delta leaves the checkpoint unchanged; generic 5xx is not permanent; the ExistingWorkPolicy choice is exercised and shown not to create duplicate parallel pipelines.
tasks.done_when: One unique note_sync pipeline exists; the worker performs the specified flow; Room stays the local SSOT for the UI; triggers are wired; no push provider or FCM exists; no A5 retry/coalescing machinery was built.

tasks.goal: A4 backend: sync tables, revision authority, change log/cursor and the /v1/sync endpoints with atomic mutation-id dedupe.
tasks.verification: Deterministic backend tests: authenticated mutation; atomic duplicate mutation dedupe; stale baseRevision -> 409; change cursor ordering; tombstone; account isolation; failed apply does not advance the checkpoint where applicable.
tasks.done_when: New migrations after V1 create only the A4 sync structures; mutation dedupe and apply share one transaction; the server is the revision authority; the cursor is monotonic and account-scoped; tombstones are not auto-purged; no attachments/collaboration/CRDT/multi-account code exists.

tasks.goal: The single Milestone verification pass, the scope/secret scans and the M2 report.
tasks.boundary: Run both frozen gates once each, write the evidence and the report. No further review, no second audit, no post-PASS cleanup, no device, no A5.
tasks.verification: Backend: cd /mnt/AndroidDev/Projects/KeepLab-Relay && ./gradlew -p backend test build (ONCE). Android: cd /mnt/AndroidDev/Projects/KeepLab-Relay && ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug (ONCE). On failure, read the failure once, fix the failed path only and rerun only the failed task.
tasks.done_when: Both gates PASS, the frozen inputs re-hash byte-identical, the scope scan shows changes only inside allowed_paths, the secret scan is clean and no token plaintext was written, and the M2 report records the result. PASS means STOP.

mandatory_gates.name: BACKEND
mandatory_gates.note: Run once, after A3 and A4 are complete. Do not re-run after PASS. Do not re-run the Android side because the backend side passed, or vice versa.

mandatory_gates.name: ANDROID
mandatory_gates.note: Device-free. No connectedAndroidTest, no benchmark module, no APK install.

optional_checks.runs: at most ONCE, only if a container runtime or a local PostgreSQL is genuinely available and the check is cheap
optional_checks.note: Absence never blocks M2 and must never be replaced by an infrastructure installation effort. The transaction design must not be weakened because the runtime is unavailable.

verification_intent.oracle_intent: Assert on deterministic, machine-readable evidence only: the backend Gradle build/test result, the Android unit-test and assembleDebug result, HTTP status and body of the auth and sync routes under the in-process test host, the presence/content of the migrations and the Room outbox/checkpoint structures, the sha256 identity of the frozen inputs, the scope scan and the secret scan. No visual judgement, no LLM judgement, no screenshot, no device.
verification_intent.fixture_intent: Fakes and in-process doubles only: a fake email/verification sender, an injectable session/refresh service boundary, a fake database readiness probe, a fake backend or Ktor MockEngine for the Android sync client, and deterministic time. No live PostgreSQL, no live server, no device, no network.
required_checks: opaque refresh token works and is stored only as a verifier
retry-safe refresh rotation works (same token + same refresh_request_id -> same result)
AUTH_REQUIRED does not delete local data
pre-login LOCAL_ONLY data is not silently adopted
failed delta does not advance the checkpoint
404 does not delete a live local row
no token plaintext in reports, evidence or logs
not_verified_here: any live PostgreSQL behaviour beyond the optional single check
Android device behaviour of any kind

stop_conditions: Any required write falls outside allowed_paths or targets a forbidden path: STOP and emit CONTRACT_DEVIATION.
Any frozen_inputs file has drifted: STOP and emit STALE_M2_INPUT.

The independent backend project cannot work without changing a repository-root Gradle file, or the Android side needs a change to settings.gradle.kts / build.gradle.kts / gradle.properties / the wrapper: STOP and emit M2_ROOT_GRADLE_CHANGE_REQUIRED with the exact file and change; do not make the change.

A needed Android change falls outside the enumerated surface (for example a theme, a shared UI widget, a resource file, androidTest, benchmark or a Room schema export): STOP and emit M2_SURFACE_BROADENING_REQUIRED with the exact file and reason; do not broaden silently.
Any Google login, Google Identity, Firebase Auth, Google private API, phone auth or OAuth social login is needed or appears: STOP.
Credential Manager would be used as an identity authority or with a Google ID credential: STOP — it is password credential UX only.
A real secret would have to be written, committed or echoed into evidence, or a token/password/OTP/refresh secret would be logged: STOP.
account deletion would have to be implemented: STOP — D-05 is pending and account deletion is out of scope.
automatic Trash expiration/purge or automatic tombstone purge would have to be implemented: STOP — D-06 is pending and out of scope.
A push provider, FCM or a background push architecture would be needed: STOP.
An attachment, object-storage or collaboration feature would be needed: STOP.
A6 conflict-resolution UI, A5 retry/coalescing machinery, manual-retry UX, process-death hardening or lost-wakeup hardening would be needed: STOP — those belong to A5/A6.
Full Room database encryption (or an SQLCipher-style dependency) would be introduced or claimed: STOP — no database-encryption feature is authorized.
A passkey would be implemented: STOP — deferred.
The Android device would have to be touched, or adb, Maestro, UiAutomator, an instrumentation run or an APK install used: STOP; M2 is device-free.
Any Tencent Cloud resource would have to be provisioned, any cloud credential used, or any production deployment performed: STOP.
Hermes configuration, the hook allowlist, Hermes core, contract_guard.py, the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract, an A0/A1/A2 package or this package would have to be modified: STOP.
The contract package manifest does not verify: STOP.
The M2 session would have to broaden its own allowed paths: STOP; a new human-approved contract is required.
The session is about to stop after A3: STOP — A3 is a checkpoint, not a stop; continue directly to A4.
An A3 contract, an A4 contract, an A3/A4 review or a post-PASS audit is being created: STOP — one milestone contract, one session, one verification pass.
A gate fails and the fix would reach outside allowed_paths: STOP.
The same failure survives two genuine fixes: STOP and perform ONE root-cause analysis; do not restart M2 from zero.
More than roughly 30 tool calls have occurred before meaningful product writes without a real blocker: STOP overhead work and execute (PROCESS_OVERHEAD_TOO_HIGH).
A minor wording, naming or warning issue is being turned into a new contract: STOP — append it compactly to reports/KEEPLAB-MINOR-BACKLOG.md instead.

failure_rule.rule: Read the failure once, fix the failed path only, rerun only the failed task. Do not restart M2 and do not re-run tasks that already passed.
failure_rule.repeated_failure: If the same failure survives two genuine fixes: emit REPEATED_FAILURE and perform one root-cause analysis.
failure_rule.allowed_patch_surface: Only files inside allowed_paths may be edited to fix a failure. A fix that would need a root Gradle change, a forbidden Android file or a new dependency outside the backend/Android dependency surface is a STOP, not a workaround.
failure_rule.gate_rule: Do not re-run the already-passed gate side. A backend failure never justifies re-running the Android gate, and an Android failure never justifies re-running the backend gate.

overhead_rule.statement: M2 is a large milestone and implementation may naturally take time, but process overhead must not dominate.
overhead_rule.rule: After contract activation and the stale-input check, begin implementation immediately. If more than ~30 tool calls occur before meaningful product writes without a real blocker: PROCESS_OVERHEAD_TOO_HIGH — simplify and execute.

non_goals: A5 offline hardening (bounded retry, manual retry UX, coalescing, process-death hardening, lost-wakeup hardening)
push provider, FCM and background push architecture
Google login, Google Identity, Firebase Auth, Google private API
changing the root Android Gradle surface
Google Keep work of any kind
editing the frozen P0B-CLOSE contract, an A0/A1/A2 package or this package
editing contract_guard.py, the hook configuration or Hermes core
re-writing D-01/D-04/D-10 in stale reports outside this milestone

decisions.statement: M2 is executed as ONE milestone with ONE contract, ONE execution session and ONE final verification pass: A3 -> A3 light checkpoint -> A4 -> verify once.
decisions.rationale: Phases are checkpoints, not bureaucratic stops. Separate A3/A4 contracts, reviews and post-PASS audits add overhead without adding a verifiable outcome.

decisions.statement: The Android write surface is enumerated, not the whole app: the data/di/model packages, the auth- and note/label/checklist-relevant UI packages, the application/activity entry points, AndroidManifest.xml, app/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/src/test/**.
decisions.rationale: A3/A4 genuinely need new packages plus edits to the single repository/creation boundary, DAOs, database, DI, navigation and the UI that calls them — which justifies a real Android surface — while themes, shared widgets, resources, androidTest, benchmark and schemas are provably unrelated to M2 and stay blocked.

decisions.statement: The root Android Gradle surface is unchanged; only app/build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml may change, and only to add M2 dependencies.
decisions.rationale: A dependency addition is an ordinary module-level change. Nothing M2 needs justifies touching settings.gradle.kts, the root build file, gradle.properties or the wrapper.

decisions.statement: The backend extends the existing independent Gradle project and the frozen Kotlin/Ktor/PostgreSQL stack; new domain tables arrive as new Flyway migrations after V1.
decisions.rationale: A2 is PASS and re-opening it would be a regression. Flyway is already wired with migrate-on-start, so A3/A4 only add migrations and services.

decisions.statement: Passwords use a vetted modern password KDF (Argon2id preferred). Verification and reset codes are stored only as secure verifiers with fixed TTL/attempt/cooldown limits, and a delivery abstraction with a fake sender keeps the flow deterministic.
decisions.rationale: D-01 requires email verification without choosing a production email vendor. Storing only verifiers and using a fake sender keeps A3 deterministic and secret-free.

decisions.statement: Refresh rotation is retry-safe through refresh_request_id with a bounded replay window, implemented with the smallest safe design: either deterministic re-derivation of the child credential from server-side secret material plus the presented parent credential and the request id, or an encrypted-at-rest retained result. No plaintext token is ever stored or logged.
decisions.rationale: D-10 requires a lost response to recover the same rotated result without minting multiple valid child sessions or destroying account access, and forbids plaintext refresh secrets at rest.

decisions.statement: Android session material lives only in an app-private, Android Keystore-backed secure store; Room is not encrypted and no encrypted-database claim is made.
decisions.rationale: D-10 plus §9 of the architecture spec require secure app-private storage with Keystore where appropriate; D-04 explicitly forbids claiming full Room encryption.

decisions.statement: D-04 is implemented as a non-destructive sign-out with account-scoped filtering: signed-out shows LOCAL_ONLY only; signed-in shows LOCAL_ONLY plus the active account's rows; another account's rows stay cached but hidden and never sync.
decisions.rationale: It is the literal D-04 decision and it keeps single-active-account phase-1 semantics without deleting anything.

decisions.statement: Pre-login LOCAL_ONLY notes are never adopted automatically; new notes created while signed out stay LOCAL_ONLY and new notes created while signed in become account-scoped SYNC_PENDING. No bulk-link feature is built.
decisions.rationale: MISSION.md invariant 1 forbids silently assigning, uploading, deleting or merging an existing local note into an account. Leaving them LOCAL_ONLY is the fastest safe behaviour.

decisions.statement: Room moves directly to the next clean schema version by an experimental schema bump with DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES; no migration chain is authored and local Long primary keys are kept where they remain useful.
decisions.rationale: Project data is disposable experimental data (CLEAN_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE > OLD_TEST_DATA_COMPATIBILITY), and MIG-1/MIG-2 allow the local PK to remain an implementation-local identity.

decisions.statement: The outbox is a persistent Room table written in the same transaction as the entity mutation, carrying mutationId, accountId, target client UUID, mutation kind, baseRevision, a captured payload and createdAt plus only the minimal A4 status fields.
decisions.rationale: OUT-1 and the architecture data model require one local transaction; anything more (coalescing, bounded retry, manual retry) belongs to A5.

decisions.statement: The dedupe claim, the mutation apply, the revision increment and the change-log append share one server-side transaction, and a duplicate mutation_id returns the already-applied result.
decisions.rationale: This is the FROZEN §4.1 consistency boundary; anything narrower would allow a double-apply or a lost delta.

decisions.statement: The server is the revision authority and the only conflict clock: stale baseRevision yields 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, the client marks CONFLICT and stops destructive overwrite, and no client wall clock is ever used for ordering.
decisions.rationale: REV-1 plus the server-clock rule; A6 owns any resolution UI, so M2 stops at the CONFLICT state.

decisions.statement: Trash and tombstone stay distinct; M2 never auto-purges Trash or tombstones.
decisions.rationale: TRASH-1/TRASH-2 and D-06 being pending; automatic retention would pre-empt an unmade human decision.

decisions.statement: The client checkpoint advances only after a clean transactional apply of the returned delta page; a failed delta leaves it unchanged.
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT CUR-1; advancing early would silently drop a delta.

decisions.statement: A 404 from the server never deletes a live local row; it maps to a non-destructive sync/error state.
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT ERR-3: a 404 may mean a stale id, an authorization mismatch, compaction or a protocol mismatch.

decisions.statement: Any entity in a remote-sync state has a non-null accountId; LOCAL_ONLY is the only state that permits a null accountId.
decisions.rationale: INVARIANT ISO-1b, enforced at creation/update boundaries and by deterministic tests.

decisions.statement: One unique WorkManager note_sync pipeline with NetworkType.CONNECTED; the exact ExistingWorkPolicy is an A4 implementation decision proven by deterministic tests against the actual WorkManager version.
decisions.rationale: The architecture spec deliberately does not freeze KEEP vs APPEND_OR_REPLACE, and forbids multiple simultaneous sync workers.

decisions.statement: Verification is ONE pass with both gates run once each; a failure fixes the failed path and re-runs only the failed task; PASS means STOP.
decisions.rationale: Milestone execution: no review of review, no post-PASS audit, no re-run of a passing task.
